literal: All lamps are not lamps; to the noble, the unlying lamp indeed is the lamp.
translation: All external lamps that shed light are not true lamps; to the virtuous, the lamp of truthfulness, which never lies, is the only true lamp.
modern: புற இருளை நீக்கும் எல்லா விளக்குகளும் உண்மையான விளக்குகள் அல்ல; சான்றோர்களுக்குப் பொய் சொல்லாத வாய்மை என்னும் விளக்கே உண்மையான விளக்காகும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts physical lamps with the spiritual light of truthfulness. The poet states that ordinary lamps, which merely dispel physical darkness, are not considered true lights by noble minds. For the virtuous, the only real lamp is truthfulness, referred to here as the 'unlying lamp' (poyyā viḷakku). While physical lights can be extinguished and only illuminate the outside, the light of truth shines eternally within, guiding a person's character and dispelling the darkness of ignorance and falsehood.
